prompt: Under twelve-tone equal temperament with MIDI note 69 at 440 Hz, what changes when a note number increases by 12?

options.text: The frequency doubles and the phase increment doubles at the same sample rate.
options.explanation: Correct. Twelve semitones form one octave. The exponential mapping doubles the frequency, and dividing by the unchanged sample rate doubles the increment.
Equal temperament uses frequency ratios. A fixed difference in hertz does not preserve the same interval at every pitch.
The sample rate is a system setting; musical note changes alter the oscillator increment.

options.text: The oscillator must reset its phase to zero.
options.explanation: Changing the increment does not require a phase reset. Keep the ongoing phase to preserve continuity.

workedExample: MIDI note 69 is 440 Hz under the stated reference. Note 81 is twelve semitones higher, so it is 880 Hz. At 48 kHz their phase increments are approximately 0.00917 and 0.01833 cycles per sample. The second step advances twice as far without resetting phase.
